correctness.rationale: For the coefficient vector (-cos θ,1)/sqrt(1+cos²θ), the smallest singular value is at most sin θ||Y||/sqrt(1+cos²θ), while the largest is at least ||X||. Thus κ<=K forces ||X||<=K θ||Y||. Set X=θ z. Event indicators converge a.e. to κ([z,z+Y])<=K, since the boundary for fixed nonzero Y is a proper algebraic null set. The integrals have envelope ||f||∞ Vol(B_k(K||Y||)), integrable by E||Y||^k<infty. A right orthogonal two-column rotation reduces the matrix to [r,Y/sqrt2]; the Jacobian produces 2^-k||Y||^k times the volume for [r,e1]. The latter has Gram determinant b² and trace 1+a²+b², so condition κ<=K is b∈[1/K,K] and a²<=(K-b)(b-1/K), yielding V_k by polar coordinates. Independently checked exact k=2/3 Gaussian constants via symbolic integration for K=3/2 and 5/2. Gaussian X f(0), χ_k moment give stated Gaussian specialization. The limit is fixed k,K only and finite numerical experiments are supplementary.

final_claim: For fixed real k>=2 and K>1, independent X,Y in R^k with globally bounded X-density f continuous at zero and E||Y||^k<infinity, M_theta=[X,cos(theta)X+sin(theta)Y] has theta^-k P(kappa_2(M_theta)<=K) -> 2^-k f(0)E||Y||^k V_k(K) with V_k(K)=4*pi^((k-1)/2)/Gamma((k-1)/2) integral_{1/K}^K b^(k-2)sqrt((K-b)(b-1/K))db.
limitations: Only fixed k,K, independent real sketch columns; no structured dependent sketches, finite θ error or whole-algorithm stopping distribution.
Finite E||Y||^k and bounded origin-continuous density are essential to dominated convergence.
